questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: In wedge frame, effective $g$ normal to incline $=g\cos\theta-\frac{g\cot\theta}{2}\sin\theta=\frac{g\cos\theta}{2}$. Normal speed $=u\sin45^\circ$, so $T=\frac{2u/\sqrt2}{g\cos\theta/2}=\frac{2\sqrt2\,u}{g\cos\theta}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $[\alpha]=MT^{-2}$, $[K]=ML^2T^{-2}$. $\frac{\alpha K^2}{\sqrt\beta}=[F]\Rightarrow\sqrt\beta=M^2L^3T^{-4}\Rightarrow\beta=M^4L^6T^{-8}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: Minimum speed to reach $(x,y)$: $u^2=g\left(y+\sqrt{x^2+y^2}\right)=9.8\times18\Rightarrow u=13.28$ m/s. Any $u\ge13.28$ m/s can reach it.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: Intersection $A=(d/2,\sqrt{R^2-d^2/4})$, $v_A=\frac{vR}{2y}=\frac{v}{2\sqrt{1-(d/2R)^2}}\Rightarrow k=2$.

questions.subject: Physics
options: Angle of the plane surface with +x axis is $90^\circ+\tan^{-1}\!\left(\tfrac13\right)$.
Angle of the plane surface with +x axis is $\tan^{-1}\!\left(\tfrac13\right)$.
Direction of change in momentum makes angle $\tan^{-1}\!\left(\tfrac13\right)$ with the +x axis.
Direction of change in momentum makes angle $90^\circ+\tan^{-1}\!\left(\tfrac13\right)$ with the plane surface.
questions.solution: $\Delta\vec p=2(3\hat i+\hat j)\Rightarrow$ angle $\tan^{-1}(1/3)$ with +x. Frictionless plane $\Rightarrow\Delta\vec p\perp$ plane, so plane makes $90^\circ+\tan^{-1}(1/3)$ with +x. D is wrong ($\Delta\vec p$ is $90^\circ$ to the plane).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: Both fall freely, so collision needs relative velocity along AB: velocity of B at $120^\circ$ from +x $\Rightarrow\theta=30^\circ$. $|v_{rel}|=2(20)\sin60^\circ=20\sqrt3$, $AB=200$ m $\Rightarrow t=\frac{200}{20\sqrt3}=\frac{10}{\sqrt3}$ s.

questions.subject: Physics
options: Speed of the rain relative to the ground is $2$ m/s.
Speed of the man when he finds rain falling at $45^\circ$ with the vertical is $4$ m/s.
The man has travelled a distance of $16$ m on the road by the time he finds rain falling at $45^\circ$.
questions.solution: Rain $=(a,-a)$; man $v$: $|a-v|=a\Rightarrow v=2a$. Relative speed $a\sqrt2=2\sqrt2\Rightarrow a=2$. Rain speed $=2\sqrt2$ (B false), $v=4$ m/s, $s=\frac{v^2}{2(0.5)}=16$ m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\varepsilon_0=\frac{q^2}{F r^2}\Rightarrow M^{-1}L^{-3}T^{4}I^{2}$; $\mu_0=\frac{1}{\varepsilon_0c^2}\Rightarrow MLT^{-2}I^{-2}$. A and C are wrong.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $v_y=V_0$, $v_x=\sqrt{2gy}\Rightarrow \sqrt{2g}\,y^{1/2}dy=V_0\,dx\Rightarrow y=\frac{(3gV_0x)^{2/3}}{2g}$. So $a=3,\ b=2,\ c=3$ and $a+b+c=8$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $m\propto V^{6}g^{-3}d$ (dimensions). $\frac{\Delta m}{m}\approx6\times1\%=6\%$ (exact $1.01^6-1=6.15\%$, also accepted).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: Limiting path grazes edge B: $\tan\theta=\frac43$, so at B $v_x=60$, $v_y=80$ m/s downward. Fall 960 m: $960=80t+5t^2\Rightarrow t=8$ s. $OP=60\times8=480$ m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\sigma=\frac{R\pi r^2}{l}$: $\frac{\Delta\sigma}{\sigma}=\frac{2}{64}+2\left(\frac{0.02}{0.26}\right)+\frac{0.1}{156}\approx18.6\%$. $\frac{x}{3}\approx6.2\to6$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $2t+3n=25$ and distance $=500$ m $\Rightarrow 5t^2+15tn=500$. Solving, $t=5$ s, $3n=15$, $n=5$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: Horizontal: $-v\sin\theta\,t+\tfrac12at^2=0\Rightarrow t=\frac{2v\sin\theta}{a}$. Vertical: $h=v\cos\theta\,t+\tfrac12gt^2=\frac{2v^2}{a}\sin\theta\left(\cos\theta+\frac{g}{a}\sin\theta\right)$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: Boat w.r.t. ground $=10\hat i+6\hat j$. Apple meets cyclist after 4 s: $4(10+v_x)=80\Rightarrow v_x=10$; $4(6+v_y)=60\Rightarrow v_y=9$; same horizontal plane $\Rightarrow v_z=20$ ($g=10$). Sum $=39$, $39/13=3$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: A to ceiling: $20=\tfrac12(10)t^2\Rightarrow t=2$ s. After bounce it rises only 10 m back up from B, so $v'^2=2(10)(10)\Rightarrow v'=10\sqrt2$ m/s; down-and-up time $=2\sqrt2$ s. Total $=2+2\sqrt2$ s.

questions.subject: Chemistry
options: An $80$ eV electron cannot excite it to a higher state.
An electron of $8.2$ eV and a photon of $91.8$ eV are emitted when a $100$ eV electron interacts with it.
All the three other options are correct.
questions.solution: $13.6Z^2=122.4\Rightarrow Z=3$. First excitation $=122.4-30.6=91.8$ eV, so $80$ eV can't excite; $100$ eV electron leaves $8.2$ eV and the atom then emits $91.8$ eV. All correct.

questions.solution: $46x+92(1-x)=69\Rightarrow x=0.5$, i.e. 50% NO$_2$ (mole basis).

questions.subject: Chemistry
options: The equivalent weight of $Fe_{0.95}O$ is $\dfrac{M_B}{0.5}$, where $M_B$ is the molecular weight of $Fe_{0.95}O$.
The number of moles of $Fe^{3+}$ and $Fe^{2+}$ in 1 mol $Fe_{0.95}O$ are $0.1$ and $0.85$, respectively.
The number of moles of $Fe^{3+}$ and $Fe^{2+}$ in 1 mol $Fe_{0.95}O$ are $0.85$ and $0.1$, respectively.
questions.solution: $x+y=0.95$, $3x+2y=2\Rightarrow Fe^{3+}=0.1,\ Fe^{2+}=0.85$. Oxidation of $Fe^{2+}$ gives n-factor $0.85$, so equivalent weight is $M_B/0.85$ (A false).

questions.subject: Chemistry
options: The concentration of the solution remains the same.
The volume of the solution becomes $200$ mL.
The mass of $H_2SO_4$ in the solution is $19.6$ g.
questions.solution: 98% w/w with $d=0.1$ g/mL $\Rightarrow M=\frac{10\times98\times0.1}{98}=1$ M. Mixing two 1 M solutions: 1 M, $200$ mL, $0.2$ mol $=19.6$ g.

questions.subject: Chemistry
options: The nodal surface is at a radial distance of $6a_0$ from the nucleus.
The number of angular nodes in the given orbital are $2$.
questions.solution: $\psi\propto \frac{r}{a_0}\left(6-\frac{r}{a_0}\right)e^{-r/3a_0}\cos\theta$: this is $3p_z$. Radial node at $r=6a_0$; angular nodes $=l=1$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
options: The radius of the $n^{th}$ orbit is $\dfrac{n^2h^2\varepsilon_0}{200\pi m e^2}$, where $m$ is the mass of an electron, $h$ is Planck's constant and $e$ is the charge of an electron.
If all atoms are in the $16^{th}$ excited state, then during de-excitation till the $10^{th}$ excited state, the total maximum number of possible wavelengths emitted is $21$.
The wavelength of the photon emitted when transition takes place from the third excited state to the ground state is $1.21$ Å.
Since the mass of the imaginary particle is different from the mass of the electron, the velocity of the imaginary particle and the electron in the $n^{th}$ orbit will be different.
questions.solution: $r_n=\frac{n^2h^2\varepsilon_0}{\pi(50m)(4)e^2}$ ✓. $n=17\to11$: 7 levels, $^7C_2=21$ ✓. C: $E=13.6\times16\times50\times\frac{15}{16}=10200$ eV, $\lambda=\frac{12400}{10200}\approx1.216$ Å $\approx1.22$ Å (not 1.21). D: Bohr speed $v=\frac{Ze^2}{2\varepsilon_0nh}$ is independent of mass.

questions.subject: Chemistry
options: Normality of $H_2SO_4$ for neutralization is $0.2$ N.
questions.solution: Equivalents of NaOH $=26.7\times0.4/1000=0.01068$. $\frac{x}{40}+\frac{0.5-x}{49}=0.01068\Rightarrow x=0.104$ g $SO_3$ ($20.7\%$). $H_2SO_4=0.396$ g. Normality can't be fixed without volume.

questions.solution: $NH_3=0.1$ mol $\Rightarrow Mg_3N_2=0.05$ mol (uses 0.4 mol HCl). MgO uses $0.2$ mol HCl $\Rightarrow 0.1$ mol. Mg $=0.1+3(0.05)=0.25$ mol $=6$ g.

One photoelectron of zero kinetic energy is ejected.
One photoelectron is ejected, which requires a stopping potential of $5.52$ V.
questions.solution: $h\nu=4.136\times10^{-15}\times2.3\times10^{15}=9.51$ eV; $KE=5.51\approx5.52$ eV $\Rightarrow V_0\approx5.52$ V. One photon ejects one electron.

questions.subject: Mathematics
options: The total number of quadratic equations is $100$.
The number of quadratic equations with equal roots is $3$.
The number of quadratic equations with one root equal to unity is $2$.
The number of quadratic equations with one root equal to $-1$ is $9$.
questions.solution: $1+a+b>0$, so no equation has root $1$ (count is $0$, not $2$). Equal roots: $(2,1),(4,4),(6,9)$; root $-1$: $a=b+1$ gives 9. Incorrect option: C.

questions.solution: Denominators $=\frac32(n+1)(n+2)$, term $=\frac{2}{3}\left[\frac1{n+1}-\frac1{n+2}\right]\Rightarrow S=\frac23\cdot\frac12=\frac13$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution: $\sum\frac1{x_i}=\frac{3p}{2p}=\frac32$ and $\sum x_i=6$: AM $=2=$ HM $\Rightarrow x_1=x_2=x_3=2$. Value $=\sin^{-1}1+\cos^{-1}1-\tan^{-1}1=\frac\pi2+0-\frac\pi4=\frac\pi4$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution: A (Cauchy), B (Nesbitt), D (AM–HM) are true. C: AM–GM gives $\prod(1+x)\ge8\sqrt{xyz}=8$, so '$<8$' is false. Incorrect option: C.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution: $b=\text{HM}<\text{GM}<\text{AM}<\text{power mean}$, so $\frac{a^p+c^p}{2}>b^p$ for every $p>1$. All four true.

questions.subject: Mathematics
options: If $a\ge b>1$, then the largest possible value of $\log_a\!\left(\dfrac ab\right)+\log_a\!\left(\dfrac ba\right)$ is $0$.
The number of integers $b$ for which $\log_b2024$ is a positive integer is $0$.
There is a unique positive integer $n$ such that $\log_2(\log_{16}n)=\log_4(\log_4n)$. The sum of the digits of $n$ is $13$.
The set of real numbers $x$ for which $\log_{2024}\log_{2023}\log_{2022}\log_{2021}\log_{2020}x$ is defined is $\{x\mid x>c\}$. Then $c=2020^{2021^{2022}}$.
questions.solution: A: sum $=\log_a1=0$. B false: $b=2024$ gives $\log_b2024=1$. C: $n=256$, digit sum $13$. D: peeling the logs gives $x>2020^{2021^{2022}}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution: $x^2-3x+5$ is irreducible, so both quadratics are proportional: $a+2=k$, $b-1=3k$, $c=5k$. $c-a-b=k+1\le6$, $a\ge1\Rightarrow k=3,4,5$; $a+b+c=9k-1=26,35,44$.

questions.subject: Mathematics

The common ratio of the geometric progression is $\dfrac14$.
The common ratio of the geometric progression is $\dfrac12$.
The common difference of the arithmetic progression is $26$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution: $\int_0^4f=\int_0^2[f(x)+f(x+2)]dx=4\Rightarrow k=0$. $\alpha=\beta=\frac12\Rightarrow q=1$. Roots of $(1-a^2)x^2+2ax-1$ are $\frac1{a+1},\frac1{a-1}$; both in $(0,1)\Rightarrow a>2$. Least $a=3$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution: First term $1-r$, second $r(1-r)$, third $r^2(1-r)=\frac18\Rightarrow r=\frac12$ or $\frac{1\pm\sqrt5}{4}$. Distinct series: $r=\frac{1+\sqrt5}{4}$, second term $\frac{\sqrt5-1}{8}$. $m=5,n=1,p=8\Rightarrow518$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution: At $x=1$ both bounds equal 1 so $P=1+A(x-1)^2$, $1\le A\le2$. $P(11)=100A+1=181\Rightarrow A=\frac95$. $P(16)=225\cdot\frac95+1=406$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution: Particular solution $a_n=-2n$; $a_n=C\cdot3^{n-1}-2n$, $a_1=1\Rightarrow C=3$. $a_n=3^n-2n\Rightarrow a_{100}=3^{100}-200$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution: $a_{200}+400=3^{200}$; powers of 3 end in 3,9,7,1 (cycle 4) and $200\equiv0\pmod4\Rightarrow$ last digit $1$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution: $P=ax^2+bx+c$: relation gives $a=1$; $P(0)=8\Rightarrow c=8$; $P(2)=32\Rightarrow b=10$. Sum of coefficients $=P(1)=19$.
